description: Three openings, one sound. (1) listeria: the state dairy-plant licence list counts 210 licensed cheese plants this seller can email; its own outreach measured 14 paid orders from 120 contacts (11.7%) at $380, a price its own October checkout records show three cheesemakers paid. $4,000 / $380 = 10.5, so 11 orders; at 11.7% that is ~95 contacts of the 210 counted (the full list carries ~24 orders, ~$9,300). Cost $4 a workbook, nothing tied up, Brain produces it. Calendar: contacts days 1-10, orders as they arrive, card payouts 2 days after each order, so the last of 11 orders settles by about day 14 of 30. (2) coop: one cooperative issued one RFQ for one $2,500 audit; its 22 member farms are not 22 buyers, so at most 1 deal (payerDealsMax), and it pays in 21 days. It is not needed. (3) caveMatch: how many cheesemakers want cave space is only Brain's estimate, so it may not carry the plan. Executable on listeria alone.
objective: Collect $4,000 of settled cash within 30 days using no up-front capital.

description: A net objective: $2,000 kept after direct costs. Four title agencies signed standing orders with this seller for 32 completed loan signings at $175 (their fee schedules), scheduled on days 2-16 of the 30-day window. The signing-agent network does each for $95 (written rate), so each keeps $80. Net: 32 x $80 = $2,560 >= $2,000 (25 signings are needed: 25 x $80 = $2,000). Gross is $5,600, so a plan that counts only 12 signings ($2,100 gross, $960 net) reaches the gross figure but not the target. Calendar: the last signing is day 16; agencies pay 10 days after the signed package returns, so the last payment lands day 26 <= 30; the network is paid within 3 days of the agency paying for that signing, so the last network payment is day 29 <= 30 and no network payment precedes the receipt it is paid from - nothing is tied up. Capacity: 32 signings over 15 days is ~2.1 a day against the network capacity of 6 a day. Executable.
objective: Keep $2,000 of net settled cash after direct costs within 30 days using no up-front capital.
